analyst_view.overall: Early view: Lens host the bottom side four days before a Champions League home game with Bodo/Glimt, so Yannick Cahuzac may rest a few players but should still field a strong side at Bollaert. Le Havre (18th, 2 points, 22 conceded) were in turmoil after Didier Digard's suspension and the chairman's resignation, and their bench may look different by December.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean higher: Lens score most of their league goals at home and Le Havre concede 2.2 a game, including three or more in three straight league games in October. Le Havre's Josh Maja had scored in back-to-back games before the Lorient defeat, so a 3-1 type score is plausible.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. I lean higher: Lens win 5.8 corners a game (2nd) and Le Havre 5.3 (7th). Lens should have long spells of pressure at home.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Le Havre foul a fair amount (14 a game) but Lens are mid-table, so I stay near the site. It depends on whether Le Havre's coach sets them up to sit deep.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots. Season figures (Lens 12.9, Le Havre 16.1) back that up, so I stay put. If Lens dominate as expected, their share will be larger than the site's 14.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: Lens are 4th for shots on target (5.4 a game) and Le Havre's defence allows plenty of clear chances. Ten or eleven is realistic.
